origin.description: Write each string as a line in the requested encoding.
origin.usage: stri_write_lines(str, con, encoding = "UTF-8", sep = "\n", fname = con)

arguments.name: con
arguments.text: A path or a binary connection.

arguments.name: encoding
arguments.text: The output encoding. The default is UTF-8.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: The separator joined after each string.

origin.details: The strings are joined with sep and collapse empty, then encoded and written with writeBin. A missing joined string cannot be written.
origin.example: path <- tempfile(); stri_write_lines(c("a", "b", ""), path); cat(paste0("stri_write_lines(c(\"a\", \"b\", \"\"), path) writes ", length(readBin(path, "raw", 20)), " bytes.\n"))

translation.description: Write each string as a line in the requested encoding.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string or a list of strings.

arguments.name: encoding
arguments.text: The output encoding. The default is UTF-8.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: The separator. None uses a newline.

translation.details: The strings are passed to stri_join with the separator as its own argument and collapse empty. A missing joined string raises ValueError. The return value is None.
translation.example:
import tempfile
path = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False).name
stri_write_lines(["a", "b", ""], path)
print(f"stri_write_lines(['a', 'b', ''], path) writes {len(Path(path).read_bytes())} bytes.")
